theron03.title: The Contract
theron03.e01.hint: The house of a patrician who pays to be remembered. Look around the room (E) and go to him.
theron03.h.mosaic.1: A mosaic on the floor: the three Fates spinning. The one with the shears was torn out, stone by stone, and a smiling goddess put in her place.
theron03.h.urn.1: A lead urn, sealed with red wax. Too cold for this room. When he touches it, he smells burnt thread.
theron03.d01: The man no one remembers. I had to pay three times for someone to remember you long enough to bring you here.
theron03.c_pose: He speaks like someone who already knows the answer.
theron03.c_pose.provoke: "You paid three times to remember me. You should have haggled."
theron03.c_pose.silent: Keep quiet and let him talk.
theron03.c_pose.urn: Look at the urn while he talks.
theron03.d_pose1: I don't haggle. I pay the price and collect double later. You'll learn that.
theron03.d_pose2: A man who listens. Rare. Expensive. All the better.
theron03.d_pose3: Beautiful, isn't it? Don't touch. Not yet.
theron03.t01: A patrician who knows what I am. Or pretends very well.
theron03.d_alert: The College is nervous. Knocking under the Temple, a monster in the galleries, swindles at the port. Nervous people pay well to have things settled quietly.
theron03.gh: what is the patrician tied to?
theron03.d_threat_gone: There was a net woman at the port who said your name. She vanished this week. Clever. But clever people always come back.
theron03.t_c02: I've taken things from people since no one has remembered me. This is just one more.
theron03.t_c02.second: And every thing I take carries a piece of my name with it. How many pieces are left?
theron03.t_c02.known: Iante. The woman from Corinth, with the son with a fever. This is not just one more.
theron03.c02.ask_up: "Your threads rise to the ceiling, patrician. Who holds the other end?"
theron03.d_ask_up: I looked at your threads. They aren't tied to anyone down here. They rise to the ceiling. Who holds the other end?
theron03.d_ask_up2: ...You saw. Then you know why I cannot refuse this job. And why you shouldn't either.
theron03.d02: You sold someone a way through the galleries. I was the one who bought it. Now I want the rest: that urn must reach the underside of the Temple of the Flame, through the port tunnel.
theron03.d03: The tunnel only opens with the key of a shrine of Hestia. A pilgrim from Corinth has it, one Iante. She won't hand it over. You'll take it from her.
theron03.mread.none: Found no thread at all on the patrician.
theron03.d_read: He looks for the patrician's threads and finds none. Or almost: thin threads rising from the man's chest and vanishing into the ceiling, as if someone up there held the other end.
theron03.t_read: This man isn't tied to anything. Or he's tied to something far too big.
theron03.d_read2: You've gone pale. Forgot what you were going to say? I forget nothing. Not even you.
theron03.d_threat: Oh, and there's the net woman at the port who says your name. Curious. People like that end up catching the College's attention.
theron03.t_threat: He knows about Nerea. So this isn't a request.
theron03.c01: He waits, wine in hand, for the answer of a man with no choice.
theron03.c01.remember: "Say my name, since you remember me."
theron03.d_price: Double, then. Money is the cheapest part of this job.
theron03.d_urn: Ashes. The remains of an old mistake. You don't need to know whose.
theron03.d_remember: ...Your name. It's here, on the tip of my tongue. Funny. It doesn't matter. I know what you are, and that's enough.
theron03.c02: The urn, the key and the net woman, all on the same table.
theron03.c02.accept: Take the job and take the key from Iante.
theron03.c02.double: Take it, and plan to betray the patrician at the delivery.
theron03.d_accept: I knew you understood business. Tomorrow night, at the port.
theron03.t_accept: One more mother, one less name. I've done worse. I don't quite remember when.
theron03.d_double: Excellent. Tomorrow night, at the port. And, Théron... I read people too.
theron03.t_double: He said my name. He shouldn't be able to.
theron03.d_refuse: A pity. Then another man will fetch the key. One less gentle than you.
theron03.t_refuse: Refusing was never the end of a problem. Only the start of another.
